title: Profile-First Model Selection for Specialized Image Annotation: A Handball Knowledge Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
content: Selecting vision-language models to annotate specialized-domain images requires evidence that general-purpose benchmarks may not provide: current domain knowledge, correct domain con-cepts, and restraint where the image is inconclusive. We present a profile-first protocol for pre-deployment evaluation and instantiate it as the Handball Knowledge Benchmark (HKB). HKB separately evaluates productive terminology, rules and tactics, and both general and hand-ball-specific interpretation of images. Diagnostics cover rule currency, answer-order robustness, fabrication and warranted abstention. A provider-diverse judge panel with provider-aware recusal scores open-ended responses. Among the 19 ranked multimodal candidates, GPT-5.6 Sol led all four dimensions (G1 0.97, G2 98.8%, G3 8.22/7.98), but below it ranks order depended on dimension weighting. Diagnostics exposed mismatches hidden by aggregate scores: high rules accuracy coex-isted with superseded rule knowledge, reliable sport recognition with scarce warranted abstention under ambiguity, and near-identical general visual scores with a 1.6-point gap in handball-specific interpretation. Results were stable across judges and aggregation rules. Under an illustrative deci-sion rule, six admissible candidates differed about threefold in inference cost. Therefore, we suggest displaying domain competencies as a profile and not as a rank, while the protocol can be transferred to other domains by replacing the handball content.
